answer.evidence: The pedestal is the only base volume. It is about 10 px wide and spans rows 54-62. Its light top (rows 54-56, about 2-3 rows) is a flat light band with no clear front-edge line or eave shadow, and no ellipse. It reads as a rim or the upper part of the face. The front face is rows 57-62 with a blue panel. The post and crossarm are drawn only as thin vertical or front-facing strips. The lanterns (rows 29-42) are front-facing, with a gold crown and a blue band at rows 31-33 but no visible top plane. Nothing shows a horizontal surface seen from above, so this is a front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The lamp is thin and small, and the board image is low-resolution, so this is a judgment by eye. The post is a dark line with only a hint of a highlight. The gold bands and star finial are each one or two pixels of a single tone. Each lantern has about three tones (dark frame, orange glass, yellow core) with no per-pixel highlight or shading. The stone pedestal is a light grey block with a shaded side, about 3 steps, and no stone grain or per-stone shading. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is not pure black, but it reads as a uniform dark line rather than tinted material tones. The 4 visible tones per tile are mostly the grass background (8% near-flat), not the prop. Beside the references (the stall at 17 and the well at 20 tones per tile, with scalloped roofs, grain and stones shaded one by one), the lamp looks like a thin sticker-like silhouette with shallow ramps and little texture. The crook lamp reference is also sparse but carries a cleaner, longer ramp. When in doubt, fail.

styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts are of little use here. The lamp is thin and sparse, and the candidate's 4 tones per tile mostly come from the grass backdrop. Judged by eye against the references, the lamp itself is shallow. The post and crossarm are a near-flat dark line with little highlight/shadow banding. The stone pedestal is a flat grey block with only a small glyph, about 2-3 steps and no per-stone shading. The lanterns carry only a few warm tones, and the gold bands and star finial are tiny, with no separate light and dark steps. The dark outlines look close to neutral charcoal rather than a clear dark tint of the adjacent material. Beodeul pieces such as the well and the cheese stall show 5-6 steps per material with grain and dot texture. This lamp would look thinner and more sticker-like next to them, so it fails.
